topic: Exact degree dependence of the minimax MSE for total-treatment-effect estimation under beta-order neighborhood interference and unit-randomized Bernoulli design: prove the matched frontier R* asymp d*binom(d,k*)/n over the bounded-coefficient bounded-degree class, where k*(beta,p) is the exposed order max{k<=beta: (1-p)^k-(-p)^k != 0}, delivering both the least-favourable family and the attaining estimator, and showing that BOTH bounds of Cortez-Rodriguez, Eichhorn and Yu (JCI 2023, arXiv:2208.05553) are loose -- their d-free Theorem 2 lower bound by d^(k*+1) and their Theorem 1 d^(beta+2) variance bound by a factor d -- contrary to their printed diagnosis; verified block witness at beta=1, p=1/2 gives Theta(d^2/n) two-sidedly with no observation noise

open_problems.open_problem: For SNIPE and closely related bounded polynomial exposure estimators, what is the sharp degree-uniform variance estimator, normal-approximation rate, and largest growing-dependency regime permitting honest design-based studentization?

source_refs.claim: The paper reports that both its conservative variance estimator and worst-case bound are orders of magnitude above empirical SNIPE variance and explicitly calls for tighter variance estimation.
source_refs.author: Mayleen Cortez-Rodriguez, Matthew Eichhorn, Christina Lee Yu

source_refs.claim: The covariate-adjusted SNIPE extension gives an asymptotically conservative, less-conservative variance estimator under sparsity, not a degree-uniform sharp variance characterization.
source_refs.author: Xinyi Wang, Shuangning Li

source_refs.excerpt: o(n^(1/4)) is a sufficient Stein-bound artifact, not shown necessary; would need new lower-bound machinery
derive the proposed n^(-1/2)D_n^(3/2) rate for these bounded HT summands

open_problems.why_unsolved: The SNIPE paper's pairwise covariance completion is conservative because one assignment does not reveal joint potential outcomes, while its CLT uses generic dependency-neighborhood Stein bounds. The prior ego-polynomial review identifies the resulting degree condition as a sufficient artifact rather than a necessity theorem. When degree grows, high-order Bernoulli scores, dependency-neighborhood size, and possibly vanishing variance move together; neither the published SNIPE analysis nor the banked exposure-HT argument supplies ratio consistency, a matching Berry-Esseen lower bound, or coverage at the true minimax scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A degree-sharp conservative or ratio-consistent variance estimator, a matching Berry-Esseen upper/lower frontier in n and dependency degree, and a uniform studentized CLT with an explicit maximal growth regime and counterexample beyond it.

writing_exemplar.why: Its simulations and future-work section state the variance-estimation failure for the exact estimator class.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: SNIPE is design-unbiased -> usable inference needs assignment-based variance estimation -> current variance estimates and fixed-degree CLTs are conservative -> obtain scale-correct studentization over growing degree

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its covariance-aware conservative variance construction and studentization proof while retaining exact growing-degree and Bernoulli-score factors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is a direct inference extension of SNIPE and targets the same unobserved covariance terms.

method_exemplars.technique: Refine the dependency-graph Stein expansion using the bounded polynomial-score structure, then construct matching finite-population schedules.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its local-dependence normal approximation is the proof route behind the sufficient degree conditions whose sharpness is at issue.

open_problems.open_problem: For bounded finite-population outcomes under Bernoulli neighborhood-exposure designs on genuinely overlapping graphs, is n/chi_f(D), adjusted for exposure propensity, the minimax effective sample size for design-valid estimation and confidence intervals?

source_refs.excerpt: Test whether the lower-bound extends from disjoint clique blocks to overlapping-neighborhood graphs
specify two block-schedule priors (or an Assouad cube) ... and its Hellinger/TV calculation
A field-tier successor would need a genuinely new heterogeneous-network interval and matching weighted lower bound

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked result proves a same-class sandwich only on disjoint clique blocks, where the experiment reduces to independent rare-exposure blocks. On overlapping neighborhoods, a lower bound must isolate genuine graph dependence while retaining computable fractional-chromatic and propensity parameters. Its reviewer also found deterministic shifted schedule pairs singular once an informative block is observed, forcing fuzzy priors or an Assouad construction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matched upper-and-lower minimax theorem over a named overlapping-graph family, with an explicit fuzzy least-favourable schedule family and an estimator or interval attaining the chi_f(D)-and-propensity rate.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the canonical design-to-exposure-mapping-to-HT-estimand framing.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: randomization identifies exposure means -> inverse exposure weighting handles unequal probabilities -> overlap induces dependent rare observations -> determine the sharp graph-dependent effective sample size

method_exemplars.technique: Use the b-fold-color Holder inequality to convert exposure-dependency structure into a fractional-chromatic Bernstein upper bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the attaining mechanism whose dependence penalty the converse must match.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt fuzzy finite-population alternatives and information-theoretic lower bounds for effective-sample-size-adaptive intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest non-network template for the required least-favourable prior and matching lower bound.

open_problems.open_problem: Is the graph-only variance envelope V_env for heterogeneous-Bernoulli bipartite Hajek estimation the exact, or uniformly constant-factor, supremum of asymptotic variance over bounded centered potential-outcome schedules?

source_refs.excerpt: Investigate whether V_env is sharp or constant-factor sharp as a worst-case bounded-outcome variance envelope
add a sharpness theorem showing V_env is the exact supremum ... over bounded centered outcome schedules

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior proposal optimizes a tractable graph-only upper envelope, but centering constraints and cross-arm covariance signs couple the worst-case outcome coordinates. Without an exact or constant-factor extremal characterization, envelope-optimal assignment probabilities need not be minimax for the actual causal estimator variance; this is the design-envelope analogue of the loose SNIPE bound diagnosed by the present topic.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An equality or two-sided constant-factor theorem for sup_Y sigma^2(G,p,Y) versus V_env(G,p), including explicit least-favourable bounded schedules and the resulting certified minimax heterogeneous design.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the homogeneous-Bernoulli bipartite estimand, variance, and CLT benchmark.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: bipartite randomization identifies exposure contrasts -> homogeneous Bernoulli admits variance and CLT theory -> heterogeneous probabilities permit graph-aware precision gains -> certify whether the optimized envelope equals worst-case variance

method_exemplars.technique: Use convex duality over conservative quadratic variance bounds to prove admissibility or expose strict slack.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is likewise an estimator-class sharpness certificate for a quadratic design-based variance object.

method_exemplars.technique: Port the bipartite Hajek linearization, covariance formula, and sparse-graph CLT to the extremizing schedules.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the estimator and limit theory whose worst-case variance must be characterized.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the exact minimax MSE for TTE estimation over bounded-coefficient beta-order neighborhood-interference models under unit Bernoulli(p) randomization, and is it Theta(d*binom(d,k*)/n) for k*=max{k<=beta:(1-p)^k-(-p)^k!=0}?

source_refs.claim: Theorem 1 gives a degree-polynomial SNIPE variance upper bound, Theorem 2 gives a d-free minimax lower bound, and the paper explicitly attributes the unmatched degree dependence to weakness in the analyses.
source_refs.author: Mayleen Cortez-Rodriguez, Matthew Eichhorn, Christina Lee Yu

open_problems.why_unsolved: The published upper proof bounds score coefficients and neighborhood covariance overlaps separately, discarding exact cancellations such as even-order terms at p=1/2 and producing an extra degree factor. Its fuzzy-Le-Cam prior yields a d-free lower rate and therefore does not activate the combinatorial amplification created by overlapping neighborhoods. No cited paper matches the two sides in d or formalizes the cancellation-defined exposed order k*.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided minimax theorem with an explicit degree-amplifying least-favourable graph/coefficient family and an attaining estimator, including regime conditions in beta,p,d,n and the cancellation-defined exposed order k*.

writing_exemplar.why: It introduces the exact TTE, low-order model, Bernoulli design, and complexity narrative that the frontier result must sharpen.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: arbitrary interference makes TTE infeasible -> low-order interactions permit unbiased SNIPE -> existing upper and lower bounds do not match in degree -> determine the exact degree-and-exposed-order frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Retain the exact pseudoinverse/SNIPE score covariance instead of the triangle-inequality count, and strengthen the paper's fuzzy-Le-Cam proof with a degree-amplifying block family.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies both the estimator weights and the only lower-bound architecture for exactly this model and design.

method_exemplars.technique: Use additive-interference reductions and explicit degree-sensitive TTE variance calculations to calibrate the beta=1 least-favourable family.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its heterogeneous additive model is the nearest beta=1 structural analogue to the proposed d^2/n frontier.

open_problems.open_problem: Can TTE be estimated adaptively when the true interaction order beta is unknown, with oracle minimax risk governed by the exposed order and an honest test of the low-order restriction?

source_refs.claim: Section 7 explicitly asks for the bias/variance effects of beta misspecification and for a statistical test to choose beta or validate low-degree polynomial structure.
source_refs.author: Mayleen Cortez-Rodriguez, Matthew Eichhorn, Christina Lee Yu

source_refs.claim: The staggered-rollout analysis names optimal model selection when beta is unknown as future work.
source_refs.author: Mayleen Cortez, Matthew Eichhorn, Christina Lee Yu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Choosing beta below the truth creates omitted-interaction bias, while choosing it above the statistically exposed order adds high-variance Bernoulli scores. At symmetric p some interaction orders cancel from the TTE score, so algebraic polynomial degree and statistically relevant order differ. With only one assignment, uniform testing may also be impossible without a separation condition.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An adaptive estimator with an oracle inequality matching the beta-known minimax rate, plus either an honest separated test for interaction order or an impossibility theorem that states the indistinguishable regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its misspecification section provides the direct problem formulation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: low beta reduces variance -> beta is unknown -> underfitting biases and overfitting inflates variance -> derive adaptive estimation and honest order testing

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its Lepski-type selection rule, oracle-inequality proof, and network-dependent asymptotic normality to nested polynomial-order estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves an analogous unknown-interference-complexity adaptation problem on a known network.

method_exemplars.technique: Use nested polynomial interpolation residuals to construct separated order tests and quantify the price of model selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shares the same beta-order potential-outcome restriction but supplies repeated rollout measurements that clarify what information a test would require.

open_problems.open_problem: Over beta-order outcome models, which network-aware assignment design and estimator jointly minimize worst-case TTE MSE, and what is the matched degree-dependent design frontier?

source_refs.claim: Section 7 asks how non-Bernoulli designs can combine causal-network structure with low-order model structure.
source_refs.author: Mayleen Cortez-Rodriguez, Matthew Eichhorn, Christina Lee Yu

source_refs.claim: The general-design pseudoinverse estimator combines clustered-design and low-order variance reductions, but the paper gives bounds and candidate-clustering selection rather than a minimax design theorem.
source_refs.author: Matthew Eichhorn, Samir Khan, Johan Ugander, Christina Lee Yu

source_refs.claim: Mixed Bernoulli/cluster designs have O(d^2/n) upper and Omega(d^(3/2)/n) lower variance bounds in a linear interference model, leaving an explicit square-root degree gap.
source_refs.author: Yiming Jiang, He Wang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Current papers optimize bounds within selected clustering families or retain explicit polynomial gaps between design upper and lower bounds. None jointly optimizes assignment dependence and the low-order pseudoinverse estimator over a bounded-degree graph class. The obstacle is that a design changes both exposure information and cross-unit covariance, so minimizing a convenient variance envelope need not minimize worst-case causal risk.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax optimal-design theorem giving a constructive assignment-estimator pair and a matching lower bound over a precisely stated class of randomized designs and bounded beta-order potential outcomes.

writing_exemplar.why: It most clearly frames model-based and design-based variance reduction as complementary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: outcome structure and clustering reduce variance separately -> pseudoinverse estimation combines them -> available clustering bounds are not minimax -> characterize the optimal joint design-estimator frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its joint estimator-design rate optimization, matching lower-bound construction, CLT, and variance-estimation argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a complete rate-optimal experimental-design template under spatial interference.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the general-design pseudoinverse and its design-matrix bias/variance characterization as the attaining-estimator side.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats the identical low-order TTE model under clustered assignments.

literature_map:
Cortez-Rodriguez, Eichhorn and Yu (JCI 2023, arXiv:2208.05553) define SNIPE, prove a coarse degree-polynomial upper bound and a d-free minimax lower bound, and explicitly request tighter variance analysis, optimized designs, and beta-misspecification theory.
Their exact Bernoulli score g(S)=prod(1-p_j)-prod(-p_j) exposes order cancellations ignored when the proof bounds score terms separately.
Yu, Airoldi, Borgs and Chayes (PNAS 2022, arXiv:2205.12803) study heterogeneous additive interference and obtain TTE guarantees with historical baselines even when the network is unknown.
Cortez, Eichhorn and Yu (NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2205.14552) use polynomial extrapolation under staggered rollouts and flag unknown-beta model selection.
Harshaw, Savje and Wang (arXiv:2210.08698) give the general design-based Riesz/pseudoinverse framework, unbiasedness conditions, CLTs, and conservative variance estimation.
Aronow and Samii (AOAS 2017, DOI:10.1214/16-AOAS1005) provide exposure-mapping HT estimation, pairwise randomization variance estimators, and local-dependence CLTs.
Li and Wager (Annals of Statistics 2022, arXiv:2007.13302) show random-graph structure can make interference estimators much more accurate than worst-case graph bounds suggest.
Leung (Econometrica 2022, arXiv:1911.07085) develops approximate-neighborhood CLTs and network-HAC inference.
Leung (Annals of Statistics 2022, arXiv:2111.04219) proves rate-optimal cluster designs for spatial interference.
Ugander and Yin (JCI 2023, arXiv:2009.02297) replace fixed graph clustering with randomized clustering and improve exposure-probability variance bounds.
Eichhorn, Khan, Ugander and Yu (arXiv:2405.07979) combine low-order pseudoinverse estimation with clustered designs but do not give a matched minimax design frontier.
Jiang and Wang (arXiv:2309.00141) leave an explicit d^2 versus d^(3/2) variance gap for mixed designs.
Belloni, Fang and Volfovsky (arXiv:2212.03683) provide a Lepski-style adaptive interference estimator with oracle rates and asymptotic normality.
Wang and Li (arXiv:2509.03050) extend SNIPE with no-harm covariate adjustment and a less-conservative but still asymptotically conservative variance estimator.
Viviano (arXiv:2003.08421) studies pilot-assisted variance-optimal network designs, supplying an adjacent joint-design technique.

Its angle0_v1-v3 reviewers prescribe a fuzzy Le Cam or Assouad least-favourable family and warn that deterministic shifted pairs are singular.
